canonical_question: Would changing the surface morphology to increase roughness likely shift the peak hardness temperature away from 600 K?

question_variants.question: Would changing the surface morphology to increase roughness likely shift the peak hardness temperature away from 600 K?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The provided evidence mentions that studying the influence of roughness is a future direction but does not contain data or simulations showing how changing surface roughness affects peak hardness temperature.

answers.answer: The text indicates that the influence of roughness on wear resistance has not been studied yet and is proposed for future work. No data exists to determine if roughness shifts the peak hardness temperature.
answers.material: FeNiCrCoCu high entropy alloy coating on Cu matrix
answers.conditions: temperature controlled variable (300 K, 600 K, 900 K, 1200 K)
answers.boundary_limitation: Future work required to study influence of roughness
evidence_spans: In this study, the wear resistance of the FeNiCrCoCu high entropy alloy coating was systematically analyzed by the molecular dynamics method.
The friction and nanoindentation simulation of this coating material were carried out by controlling the ambient temperature.

The results show that with the increase of temperature, the disorder of the lattice structure increases, which leads to an increase of the tangential force and friction coefficient in the friction process.

source_evidence_spans: In the future, the influence of roughness on the wear resistance of materials can be studied by changing the surface morphology of the material
